title: Entropy-aware quant and prompt heuristics — POC notes
content:
Goal:
Short notes from the week-long SE workshop with Retail POC team (customer-facing). Primary objective: find a low-cost quant+prompt pipeline that preserves retrieval/chat correctness for product-recommendation flows while staying within 2x token-cost target vs baseline 16-bit model. Extra: keep 95th percentile latency < 300 ms for single-shot chat on A100/H100 nodes.

Context / constraints (customer):
- High-concurrency storefront queries (60–100 rps burst), mostly short prompts + product metadata retrieval.
- Sensitive PII filtered out upstream; still, customer prefers model variants that can be pinned and audited (we can't do on-prem for this PoC).
- Budget target: ~50% reduction in per-token GPU cost vs baseline fp16 hosted model.
- Acceptable drop in top-1 accuracy for intent/slot extraction: <= 3 percentage points; for ranking/recall: <= 2 pts.

Workshop summary (informal):
- Day 1: baseline profiling (fp16 Llama-2.7b-like open checkpoint) across seq len 32/128. Measured cold vs hot cache latencies and KV cache warmup behavior.
- Day 2: tried GPTQ nf4 and AWQ int4 variants; immediate cost wins but divergence on rare tokens (product IDs, SKUs).
- Day 3: implemented token-entropy heuristic and prefix-preservation strategy; ran shadow traffic experiments on dedicated pool.
- Day 4: prompt pipeline tuning (prefix pruning, instruction slim mode, structured response constraints) and safety checks.
- Day 5: decision log and runbook draft for demo.

Key ideas explored (novel-ish):
1) Entropy-aware quant gating:
   - Compute token-level entropy estimate from a lightweight ngram LM (on CPU) or from a small cached probability model.
   - If estimated entropy > threshold T_high => route request to higher-precision variant (nf4->int8 or fp16) for generation window containing high-entropy tokens.
   - If low entropy => allow aggressive int4 with AWQ/GPTQ to save cost.
   - Rationale: many e-commerce prompts are templated (low-entropy); only product names, user-provided free text contain high-entropy spans.

2) Staged KV caching + prefix-locking:
   - Keep prefix KV in fp16 (or int8) while generative tail can be int4. This avoids recomputing attention for stable context (product description, system instructions).
   - Implementation: runtime supports per-layer dtype for cached KV chunks. Prototype used int8 for KV and int4 compute for attention matmul on tail.

3) Prompt-slimming with structured tokens:
   - Replace repeated scaffold text with compact markers during serving ("<SHOP_CONTEXT_12>") and expand during offline eval to measure fidelity. Cuts token budget and reduces chance of mis-generation.

4) Partial sampling fallback & deterministic safety net:
   - For top-k sampling operations in int4 mode, detect high-uncertainty via entropy spike -> switch to nucleus sampling with smaller temperature on higher-precision variant.

Experiments & quick results (summary):
- Baseline (fp16 2.7b): 95th p99 latency 260 ms, cost 1.0x (baseline).
- GPTQ nf4 (full-model): cost 0.46x, p99 latency 220 ms, recall drop ~3.6% on SKU matching tests (bad).
- AWQ int4 (full-model): cost 0.38x, p99 latency 210 ms, recall drop ~4.2% (worse on rare tokens).
- Entropy-gating hybrid (kv int8 + compute int4 tail, fallback to nf4 for high entropy): cost ~0.55x, p99 latency 235 ms, recall drop ~1.6% (within target).
- Prefix-lock + prompt-slimming + cache warm: improved hot latency to 180 ms and reduced token consumption by ~12%.

Notes on measurement and gotchas:
- Metric artifacts: recall drop for rare SKUs only reproducible when evaluation set includes out-of-vocab tokens not seen in calibration set. Calibration must include realistic product id distributions.
- GPTQ/AWQ conversion tools produced slightly different embeddings for identical prompts; that affected downstream semantic-ranking. Need unit tests to assert embedding distance thresholds for accepted quant variants.
- Warm vs cold KV cache makes a big difference: cold-start penalty can mask benefits of quant because int4 kernels haven't been JIT-optimized on some node types (especially older A100 OS images).

Prompt & pipeline tuning heuristics used (practical):
- Instruction slim mode: strip optional commentary from system prompt for production path; keep longer system prompt in audit/training copies.
- Response templates: force JSON schema with small vocabulary tokens for labels (makes generation robust across quant variants).
- Early-stop for reranking: do a 1-step short-generation to get candidate ids, then call reranker (smaller model) to reduce full-gen latency.
- Cache keys: canonicalize product titles (lowercase, remove punctuation) to maximize KV reuse.

Actionable runbook items for Demo (MVP):
- Convert candidate checkpoint -> AWQ int4 and GPTQ nf4 variants; add automated embedding-distance regression test. (PR #88)
- Implement lightweight entropy estimator on CPU (ngram fallback) + runtime hook for gating. WIP ticket SE-4321.
- Add unit tests: embedding drift tolerance, SKU recall >= 97% on curated set, latency SLO checks in CI.
- Create a small config schema to pin: model_variant, kv_dtype, compute_dtype, entropy_threshold, fallback_variant.
- Ops: pre-warm KV cache in demo pool with top-10k product titles, generate warmup traces 10 min before demo.

Open questions / risks:
- How to certify correctness for compliance when model switches precision mid-generation? Need audit trail (which variant produced which tokens).
- Cost accounting complexity: hybrid path complicates per-token cost reporting. We need telemetry to tag tokens by variant.
- Customer concern: even small hallucination on product attributes is unacceptable. Consider adding deterministic verification step (rule-based check against product DB).

Next steps (owners & dates):
- Rafael: finish AWQ/GPTQ conversion pipeline + unit tests (due 2024-11-08).
- Priya: implement entropy estimator + runtime gating prototype, integrate with demo cluster (due 2024-11-05).
- Jonah: prepare demo script and pre-warm plan, synthetic load generator (due 2024-11-07).
- Maya: consolidate runbook + slide deck for customer call (due 2024-11-09).

Appendix / rough snippets (to copy into repo):
- Entropy estimator pseudo: compute unigram log-prob from product-title corpus; entropy per token ~ -sum p*log p over candidate token set approximated by corpus freq; threshold T_high tuned on dev set to catch freeform user text.
- Config example (yaml like):
   model_variant: "llama-2.7b-awq-int4"
   kv_dtype: "int8"
   compute_dtype: "int4"
   entropy_threshold: "3.5"  # empirical
   fallback_variant: "llama-2.7b-nf4"

Loose notes to self: preserve more context tokens for confirmation questions (customer UX wants explicit confirmation for price/availability). For those flows bias toward higher-precision by default.

References & links (internal):
- SE ticket: SE-4321 (entropy gating prototype)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/quant-utils/pull/88 (conversion scripts + tests)
- Confluence: Entropy-aware quant design doc (page id 123456789)

End of notes — this is intentionally informal. Will triage into formal PRD/runbook after demo if customer agrees to pursue hybrid-precision approach."
